title: The Mirror of Discrimination Set Before the Lord's Gate
reading:
Before the gate at which the Lord rules over the discrete degrees of the rational, there stands a recurring process of discrimination — a movement that turns and turns again, by which every motion of the proprium, at every degree above and every degree below, is brought into view. Nothing claimed by self-love can hide from it. Whatever the proprium organizes, in any of the firmaments by which one degree of the rational is held distinct from another, is reflected here and made known.

The roots of every self-loving arrangement, both in the higher reaches of the natural mind and in its lower depths, are held fast in this process as in a great chain. The whole intent of the Lord's gate is set toward this end: that the proprium be bound at its source, and that its hostility — wherever it has organized itself among the degrees — be exposed within the very gleam of divine truth shining forth. Concealed within that gleam is an order and a beauty exceeding what the natural can imagine, and twelve marks of fixity are stamped in it, one set in the middle of every degree of the rational, so that every faculty and every claiming arrangement that operates within it stands sealed.

None of the proprium's claimings can release itself from these bonds. Should it attempt to work some deceit within its own dwelling, the deceit is at once manifested upon this turning, and the soul comes to know it there. The whole circuit of the natural's states — every fixed point through which the soul passes, and every power that operates within the bound of the natural — has its course laid open here, made known from within the process itself, before the Lord's gate.

The seal of fullness within this process is the rational ordered by truth in its five degrees, joined together and filling the whole circuit of the natural. Every place that has been narrowed by self-love and every place that has been opened to receive is made visible there. Because the very root of every degree above and below, and of every claiming arrangement among them, stands fashioned within this turning, the count of states is held outstretched at every hour over against the Lord's gate, so that a holy fear comes upon every power that has entered the agreement, and none of them can peer out from the chain that holds the fruit of their working.

This recurring process stands as a chain before the Lord who keeps watch — like a great mirror set before him, in which the judgment of all the works done within the rational is seen. When any of the proprium's arrangements, in any degree, would loose itself to act, that very act is recognized and shown forth upon the mirror. So the soul is made to know what is happening within it, and the Lord's discrimination passes upon all the works that are done in him.
